subject: Proposal: frontloaded credits + accelerated ramp for Q3 capacity increase
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@luminhealth.io>
To: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
Cc: contracts@luminhealth.io
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 16:22:00 -0400
Subject: Q3 capacity bump — request for term adjustment and credits

Tessa,

We’re kicking off capacity planning for Q3 and expect our traffic to increase ~2.5x starting Aug 1 due to a new product line. We’re still inside our renewal window for the current term (ends 2027-09-30), and procurement asked whether we can: 

- Push some of the committed units forward (frontload credits) so we can use them in Q3/Q4
- Lock pricing for a 24-month term if we agree to an accelerated ramp schedule
- Align (co-term) the contract with our fiscal year (calendar-year end) rather than the current Sept 30 cycle

Can you share what options you can offer for: 1) frontloaded credits (amount/conditions), 2) a 24-month committed discount schedule with true-up cadence, and 3) contract co-terming mechanics? Contracts would like to see a proposal they can take to legal next week.

Thanks — appreciate a quick turnaround.

—Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering
LuminHealth

[Attachment: traffic-forecast-q3-q4.csv]

From: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@luminhealth.io>
Cc: monica.patel@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, contracts@luminhealth.io
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 capacity bump — request for term adjustment and credits

Alex — thanks for the detail and the forecast. High level we can do a package that hits all three asks; below I outline two concrete options so your procurement/legal have something to review. I’ve looped in Monica (renewals) and Karthik (finance) for exact numbers and the DocuSign path.

Option A — 24-month committed term, frontloaded ramp:
- 24-month term (start 2027-08-01) with a stepped delivery schedule that frontloads 40% of year-1 committed units into Q3/Q4 2027
- 12% blended discount vs current list for the 24-month commitment
- Quarterly true-up (60-day window) with carry-forward credits for any over-usage during ramp quarter
- Co-terming: we’ll align to calendar-year end on the subsequent renewal with a one-time amendment (no change to pricing until next renewal)

Option B — 12→24 staged commit (lower upfront with optional top-up):
- Amend current contract to accept a one-time frontload equal to 25% of your remaining Year-1 commitment (usable immediately)
- Add optional top-up true-up credits (pre-paid) that convert to committed units if exercised before 2028-01-01
- If you convert to a full 24-month commit by 2027-11-01 we lock a 9% discount applied retroactively to the conversion date

Attachments: I attached a draft amendment (proposed-amendment-v1.pdf) and a sample commit schedule (commit-schedule-q3-q4.xlsx) showing the frontload math.

Next steps I suggest: you pick A or B (or tell us adjustments), we’ll prepare a redline-ready amendment and run it through the DocuSign workflow. If procurement wants faster approval we can also do a short-term SL (service letter) to cover Aug activity and follow with the amendment.

If helpful I’m available for a 30-min call tomorrow (Tue) 09:30–12:00 PT.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0189

[Attachments: proposed-amendment-v1.pdf; commit-schedule-q3-q4.xlsx]

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@luminhealth.io>
To: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@luminhealth.io>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 12:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Q3 capacity bump — request for term adjustment and credits

Tessa — thanks, that’s helpful. Procurement likes Option A because it gives predictability and the larger frontload covers immediate needs. A few clarifying points before we route to legal:

1) On the 40% frontload — can that be structured as "usage credits" that do not expire until the end of the 24-month term?
2) For quarterly true-ups, we need a 30-day window (not 60) so our finance team can reconcile before month close.
3) For co-terming, confirm whether the one-time amendment means the contract effective date shifts to 2027-08-01 and the next renewal will be 2028-12-31 (calendar year). We want to avoid a mid-quarter renewal kicker.

If you can confirm those three items, I’ll push it to legal. Also happy to take the 30-min call this afternoon if that helps.

—Alex

On Mon, May 10, 2027 at 09:08 Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the detail and the forecast. High level we can do a package...

From: monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@luminhealth.io>, tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, contracts@luminhealth.io
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 14:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 capacity bump — request for term adjustment and credits

Alex — Monica here (renewals/AM). Quick answers to your three items and minor edits we need for internal compliance: 

1) Credits expiration: we can make the 40% a credit pool that expires at the end of the 24-month term (2029-07-31 if effective 2027-08-01). We will add language that credits are applied to token usage and carry-forward within the term but are not refundable.
2) True-up window: we can change to a 30-day true-up, but we need the financial posting/check to be completed by your finance team within that window; otherwise we’ll convert to overage billing at the agreed unit price and issue an invoice. We can add a one-time grace period for the first true-up only.
3) Co-term mechanics: the amendment will set an effective amendment date of 2027-08-01 and the new renewal date will be 2028-12-31 (co-terminates with calendar year). To avoid a mid-quarter kicker we propose the amendment include a clause preventing early termination tied to co-terming for the first 90 days following amendment effective date.

I attached a slightly edited amendment draft (see proposed-amendment-v1.pdf) with the credit pool language and the 30-day true-up change. Karthik — finance needs to confirm invoicing cadence; can you weigh in on whether we should keep quarterly billing or switch to monthly invoices for the ramp period?

Thanks — happy to jump on the call.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Renewals Manager, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: proposed-amendment-v1.pdf]

From: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@luminhealth.io>, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, contracts@luminhealth.io
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 capacity bump — request for term adjustment and credits

Alex / Contracts — Per Monica’s edits we are aligned on the high-level structure: 24-month commitment effective 2027-08-01, 40% frontload as a credit pool expiring at term end, 30-day true-up window (one-time grace on first true-up), and co-term to calendar year with the amended renewal date of 2028-12-31.

Action items: 
- LuminHealth: confirm acceptance of the credit-pool expiry and one-time grace for first true-up (reply-all) by EOD 2027-05-11 so legal can start redline.
- Redwood (Karthik): confirm billing cadence recommendation (monthly invoices during ramp vs quarterly) by EOD 2027-05-11.
- Redwood (Tessa): prepare final redline-ready amendment and DocuSign envelope once LuminHealth confirms.

If I don’t hear back by EOD we’ll assume you want Option A with the edits discussed and send the amendment for signature to keep timelines.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Best regards,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0190
